scenes.heading: Workflow Model Concepts
scenes.narration: Workflows. Workflow Model Concepts. In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What is a WorkflowModel in AEM?
scenes.heading: A WorkflowModel is the definition of a workflow
scenes.body: Section 2 says a WorkflowModel is the definition of a workflow, made of nodes and transitions.

scenes.question: What is a workflow transition?
scenes.heading: A transition is the link between two consecutive steps
scenes.body: The speech defines a transition as the link between two consecutive steps, and says rules can be applied to it.

scenes.question: What nodes must every workflow model have?
scenes.heading: A model always has a start node and an end node
scenes.body: Section 2 explicitly says a model always has a start node and an end node.

scenes.question: Which payload forms are explicitly mentioned in the speech?
scenes.heading: The payload can reference a repository resource by path, UUID, or URL, or be a serialized Java object
scenes.body: Section 2 says the payload is the resource advanced through the workflow and can be referenced by path, UUID, or URL, or be a serialized Java object.

scenes.question: What does a WorkItem contain?
scenes.heading: A WorkItem contains the WorkflowData and a reference to the current WorkflowNode
scenes.body: The speech defines a WorkItem as the unit passed through a workflow instance, containing the WorkflowData and a reference to the WorkflowNode for the current step.

scenes.question: How are workflow inbox assignments described?
scenes.heading: Each user has a workflow inbox, and work items are assigned directly or through a group
scenes.body: Section 2 says each user account has its own workflow inbox, and work items are assigned either directly to a user or to a group the user belongs to.

scenes.question: Which actions are available on a workflow instance during its lifecycle?
scenes.heading: Terminate, suspend, resume, and restart are the available instance actions
scenes.body: The speech says an instance is created when you choose a model and define the payload, ends when the end node is processed, and offers terminate, suspend, resume, and restart.

scenes.heading: Quick recap
items: A WorkflowModel is the definition of a workflow
A transition is the link between two consecutive steps
A model always has a start node and an end node
The payload can reference a repository resource by path, UUID, or URL, or be a serialized Java object
A WorkItem contains the WorkflowData and a reference to the current WorkflowNode
Each user has a workflow inbox, and work items are assigned directly or through a group
Terminate, suspend, resume, and restart are the available instance actions
